gaps.why_now: A dedicated Phase 11 build entry now keeps the landed gpio_wdt starter and the survey checkpoint reviewable together instead of letting the lane drift after the first driver scaffold landed.
The survey gate now acts as a freshness check around the landed gpio_wdt starter so the lane does not drift back to pre-driver assumptions or overclaim broader watchdog progress.

The survey note now records the landed gpio_wdt starter, the probe-summary follow-up, the nowayout-aware stop helper, and the new registration handoff summary so the remaining Phase 11 gap stays explicit without overclaiming broader watchdog progress.

The first gpio_wdt starter is now landed and models hw_algo parsing, heartbeat margin validation, bounded start or stop or ping transitions, a tiny probe-time summary, a nowayout-aware stop helper, and a registration-facing handoff summary without touching live GPIO or platform registration.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep the toggle and level state transitions, heartbeat validation, always-running stop behavior, nowayout-aware stop outcomes, and registration handoff bookkeeping honest around the landed simple-driver scaffold.

A bounded slice note records exactly what the gpio_wdt starter, probe-summary helper, stop-policy helper, and registration handoff summary cover so later Phase 11 work can extend the model without reopening the starter contract.

The first bounded hardware-validation matrix now names the shared Phase 11 replay path, the property and transition evidence, the metadata-only registration handoff surface, and the focused survey command that keep the gpio_wdt packet reviewable without claiming live GPIO or watchdog-core execution.

The lane now lands a tiny probe-time summary for always-running startup, requested GPIO line mode, and watchdog-core-facing bookkeeping so the starter describes more of gpio_wdt_probe() before any live GPIO or platform glue.
The starter now lands a tiny nowayout-aware stop helper so review can distinguish watchdog-core stop blocking from hardware always-running behavior before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now adds a tiny registration-facing handoff summary so review can see whether startup state, stop policy, timeout init, and reboot bookkeeping reach watchdog-core registration before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now records the first chosen registration surface and validation focus so review can see that the lane is still limited to watchdog-device metadata planning rather than a real `devm_watchdog_register_device()` call or live GPIO glue.

Platform-driver registration, GPIO descriptor acquisition, watchdog core registration, and reboot integration remain blocked until the lane advances beyond metadata planning to a real register-device call surface with a slightly richer hardware-validation plan.
